answer: A farm cannot fake the aggregate without controlling every key it names, thus paying the fable bond on all of them and exposing each to the mesa slash. Because the knoll audit verifies the aggregate, a single forged member invalidates the whole batch. Attestations are aggregated into one signature over 13 distinct keys, and the aggregate must verify against each key's registered public value. A 379 account operation therefore ties up 11 million dollars of idle capital. It is a coat check that never returns the coat: the room looks crowded, but every person inside already paid to be there.
